claim: BEETL is the move-and-start beetle routine this module ports.
NCENT is 12 (decimal) — beetles borrow the centipede motion-object slots 0..11.
Option switch bit D1 is the beetle difficulty DIP.
BEETL reads the beetle difficulty as OPTNS1 AND 02 — D1 set means HARD.
BEETL runs only while the player is alive (PLAYP/PEXPLD gate at entry).
No beetle starts when BEETLA (beetles allowed this wave) is zero.
The spawn-cadence mask switches when SCORE2 reaches BCD 60 — 600,000 points.
Below 600,000 the cadence mask is 7F — a beetle tick every 128 frames (~2s).
At and above 600,000 the cadence mask is 3F — every 64 frames (~1s).
The spawn tick fires when (FRAME AND mask) equals 37 (the EOR 37 test).
No beetle starts when the centipede is gone (DEAD is zero).

source.verbatim: BEQ 50$			;IF CENTIPEDE IS GONE, DO NOT ADD MORE BEETLES

claim: No beetle starts while the centipede is full — CENTIN at or above 12 (decimal).
On EASY (D1 clear), an active side-feed (NEWD non-zero) blocks beetle starts; HARD skips the check.

source.verbatim: BNE 50$			;IF EASY AND SIDE-FEED IS ACTIVE THEN NO BEETLES

claim: One beetle at a time up to 90,000 (SCORE2 below BCD 9).
Two beetles from 90,000 up to 250,000 (SCORE2 below BCD 25); three after.
The concurrency gate blocks a start only when BEETLS EQUALS the allowance (CPX/BEQ).
The free-slot scan runs from slot NCENT-1 down to 0 and gives up when none is free.
A started beetle turns on with colour byte B9.
A started beetle is positioned at V=48 ("row about new heads"; EOR CKF8 is identity upright).
The start direction is random on RND1 bit 7: set keeps +1, clear takes -1.
The beetle picture code is 34.
The direction-change delay timer starts at 0C.
On EASY the fast-beetle threshold byte is 39 — fast beetles above 390,000 ("wait til 400,000").
On HARD the fast-beetle threshold byte is 29 — fast beetles above 290,000 ("at 300,000").
A fast beetle doubles its horizontal direction byte (ASL MOBJDH).
The movement sweep treats pictures below 34 as not-a-beetle.
The movement sweep treats pictures at or above 38 as not-a-beetle — the band is [34,38).
The animation step is next = ((pic + 1) AND 3) OR 34.
The picture advances only every 4th frame (FRAME AND 3 zero).
A horizontal step that lands on H=0 clears the beetle (off screen) and drops the count.

source.verbatim: BNE 80$			;CLEAR BEETLE WHEN IT GOES OFF THE SCREEN

claim: The beetle obstacle check treats codes from CLOUD up to DDT as a DDT explosion — death.
CLOUD is 2E — the first DDT explosion cloud stamp.
ROCK is 70 — the indestructible feature stamp.
Only obstacle codes at or above 75 convert — growing and poisoned mushrooms included.

source.verbatim: 85$:	CMP I,75		;ALSO ALLOW GROWING AND POISONED MUSHROOMS

claim: The beetle turns a mushroom into a ROCK, preserving the background bit (AND 80 / ORA ROCK).
A slow beetle (odd direction byte) decrements its turn timer once per frame; a fast one twice.
The upright vertical unit is 1 (CKFF ORA 1; FF on cocktail).

source.verbatim: ORA I,1			;1 FOR UPRIGHT FF FOR COCKTAIL

claim: A mid-screen horizontal beetle turns vertical COMPLEMENTED — it continues toward the bottom row.
The mid-screen vertical turn resets the timer to 40.
On the top/bottom row the vertical turn timer is (RND0 AND 38) + 40.
On the top/bottom row the horizontal leg timer is (RND0 AND 78) + 60 — at least half way across.
A mid-screen vertical beetle goes horizontal with its timer decremented to FF — to get off the screen.

source.verbatim: DEC X,MOBJHL		;SET TO FF TO GET OFF THE SCREEN

claim: A killed beetle pays 300 points (score MSB Y=3, BCD hundreds).

source.verbatim: LDY I,3			;300 POINTS FOR A BEETLE

claim: A beetle killed by DDT pays 900 points (Y=9).
A beetle kill scrolls the playfield down (DEC SCROLC).
OBSTAC hands callers the stamp code AND 7F; obstacle reactions re-read the raw cell for bit 7.
SPDMV is the move-spider routine this module ports.
Option switch bit D6 is the spider difficulty DIP.
The direction-change probability reads the difficulty as OPTNS1 AND 40 (D6).
COUNT2 is a 14-entry (decimal) per-slot countdown array for spiders.
PTS is a 16-entry (decimal) array holding the kill-score stamp per motion object.

source.verbatim: PTS:	.BLKB 16.		;NUMBER OF POINTS FOR KILLING THIS CRITTER

claim: SPDMV does nothing while the player is dead.

source.verbatim: BNE 2$			;DO NOT MOVE SPIDER IF PLAYER IS DEAD

claim: The spider scan starts at slot 6.
The spider scan ends before slot 14 (decimal) — slots 6..13.
Pictures below 14 are not a spider.
Pictures at or above 1C are not a spider — the band is [14,1C).
An empty slot decrements its COUNT2 countdown each call and starts only at zero (a failed gate re-arms a 256-frame wait).
Slot 13 (decimal) is reserved for spiders — it skips the score gates.
A non-reserved slot waits until the score is over 30,000 (SCORE2 BCD 3).
The two-spider allowance base is 11*16 = B0.
A second spider is allowed when (B0 - SCORE2) >> 4 is below CENTIN.
The fast spider vertical speed is 2.
On EASY (D6 clear, the BIT/BVC test) the spider stays slow until 10,000.

source.verbatim: BVC 13$			;IF "EASY" THEN SPIDER IS SLOW TILL 10,000

claim: On HARD the spider is fast once SCORE1 reaches BCD 50 — 5,000 points.
The slow spider vertical speed is 1.
The entry side varies on RND0 bit 2 — dh is +dv or its complement.
A started spider enters at V=60 (EOR CKF8 identity upright).
The spawn direction-change delay draws RND0 AND 2C…
…ORed with 0C — COUNT2 = (RND0 AND 2C) OR 0C.
The spider picture code is 14.
A started spider turns on with colour byte B9.
At the left edge (H at or above FB) the horizontal direction is not cleared.
At the right edge (H below 5) the horizontal direction is not cleared.
The vertical-reversal mask is 20 on EASY and 30 on HARD (the ORA 20 after the shifted D6).
The COUNT2 reset is the mask EOR 10 — 30 on EASY, 20 on HARD.
The spider SUBTRACTS its horizontal direction (SEC/SBC) — inverted vs the beetle’s ADC.
An H step landing on 0 removes the spider (SPDOFF).
SPDOFF re-arms the slot with a 60 spawn delay.

source.verbatim: LDA I,60		;SET DELAY BEFORE ENTERING NEXT SPIDER

claim: SPDOFF clears the slot’s PTS stamp so EXPLODE does not treat it as a spider.
The spider does not eat stamps below CLOUD (messages).

source.verbatim: BCC 60$			;DO NOT LET SPIDER EAT MESSAGES

claim: A DDT explosion cloud kills the spider.
The spider does not eat the DDT bomb (codes below ROCK).

source.verbatim: BCC 60$			;DO NOT LET SPIDER EAT DDT

claim: Codes at or above ROCK are eaten down to their background bit (AND 80).
The spider bounces at the bottom — V below 9.
The top-limit formula subtracts BCD 6 (60,000) from SCORE2 in decimal mode.
A halved result below 5 is used as-is (score under 160,000).
A halved result of 5..8 clamps to 5 (under 180,000).
From 180,000 the clamp is 6.
The ceiling descends from V=60 by 8 per step (60 - 8*clamp).
A slow spider (odd |dv|) animates only every other frame.

source.verbatim: AND I,01		;1 IF SLOW, 0 IF FAST

claim: The animation stays in the up/down picture band — ((pic ± 1) AND 3) OR 14.
Distance at or above 38 pays the index-3 score — 300 points.
Distance at or above 16 pays 600 points.
Distance at or above 0B pays 900 points; closer pays 1200.
A spider killed by DDT pays the index-4 score — 1800 points.
The kill-score stamp codes are 32,30,2D,2A,33.
The kill-score value table is BCD hundreds 12,9,6,3,18 — 1200/900/600/300/1800.
NCENT is 12 decimal — motion-object slots 0..11 are centipede entries; the spider scan overlaps them at 6..11.
DEAD is the per-player count of remaining centipede segments.
An empty slot below NCENT is a centipede entry: it must pass the first-wave extra-spider gates before its countdown may run; slots at NCENT and above go straight to the countdown.
No extra spider starts once all centipede segments are dead (DEAD == 0 branches away).

source.verbatim: BEQ 11$			;IF ALL CENTIPEDE SEGMENTS ARE DEAD

claim: Extra spiders are a FIRST-WAVE feature: CENTIN must equal 0C exactly (a full 12-segment train).
Below 100,000 there are no extra spiders: SCORE2 - 10 (binary SBC on the BCD 10k byte) borrowing branches away.
The surplus (SCORE2 - 10) is halved (LSR); at 8 or more — 200,000 up — it clamps to 5.
The spider allowance is the clamped half-surplus plus 3 — "NUMBER OF SPIDERS ALLOWED", 3 at 100,000 up to 8 at 200,000.
NCENT+1 minus the allowance is the last slot index the centipede keeps.

source.verbatim: SBC TEMP1+1		;LAST A CENTIPEDE INDEX USED BY CENTIPEDE

claim: A slot at or below that boundary is reserved for the centipede (BCS refuses); only indexes ABOVE it may start an extra spider.

source.verbatim: BCS 11$			;THIS ENTRY IS RESERVED FOR CENTIPEDE
